summary: H.264, VP9 and AV1 clips at 720p and 1080p in Chromium and Firefox ESR on the GNU root under the virtio-vga profile, frames shown and dropped and the decoder judged against the Debian reference guest's stored plays, but for Firefox's dropped frames, a limit that tests/graphics/runners/video.limits names; the runner is tests/graphics/runners/video.sh and the scenario tests/cases/machine/graphics_scenario.c

cases.behavior: Chromium plays the 10 s H.264 clip at 720p, muted and fullscreen under a headless Weston, once to warm up and three times counted, each to its end with no media error, showing at least the frames the Debian reference guest showed, dropping a median no more than the most Debian dropped in one play, and with the decoder Debian's Chromium chose

execution.cleanup: libetude-case stops the machine and removes the overlay, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot an overlay of the GNU system's disk on virtio-blk with rach2.root=ext2 and the virtio-vga display, wait for the root and the login prompt, log in as root at the console and open the framed guest channel

make /tmp/graphics and copy there from the read-only graphics data disk the runners, the guest's environment and the Debian references, owned by the test account, and mount the clips' data disk read-only at /tmp/graphics/clips
run video.sh -t -b chromium h264-720p.mp4 as the test account with GRAPHICS_CLASS=conformance and GRAPHICS_DONE=1, through the framed guest channel
run judge.py video on the clip's plays and decoders files and the Debian reference's, with video.limits
fetch the runner's output as the evidence out.tar.gz and write the host's half of the record, its load and the admission ledger's claims, as the evidence host-record

assertions.checks: the runner exits 0, having run its whole case, and prints its result line
judge.py finds the result no worse than the Debian reference guest's, stored under tests/graphics/ref/debian, and prints judge: result: pass

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case compares a QEMU guest's browser with the Debian reference guest's in the same QEMU display profile
